feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iteration 0 is the only evidence: one line-loss event per run and max_error of 0.062 to 0.065 m on all three tracks, with progress of 0.53 (oval), 0.27 (s-bend) and 0.14 (slalom). The failures happen on bends at the line edge, which points to late warning and overcorrection. The Integrator's controller for this geometry uses kp=4.0 and kd=0.6, because the Builder's lower weights (16.7 per metre) cut the steering gain sharply and would otherwise under-steer on tight bends. The controller therefore compensates for the lower sensor gain, so the sensing change is tested with a steering response close to iteration 0's. The next race decides the following step. If line_loss_events is still at least 1 on the tightest bend with max_error near 0.06 m, the row width is not the limit: move the sensors forward to y=0.08 (the allowed maximum) and keep the ±6 cm spread. If the robot completes or stays on track with max_error below 0.06 m but steering_oscillation is high, reduce the outer weights to ±0.75 and inner to ±0.375, keeping the spread. If line losses are gone but progress is still low on the slalom, the robot is too slow through bends, so keep the geometry and raise base_speed rather than changing the sensing.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events is at least 1 with max_error near 0.06 m on the tightest bend, move the sensor row forward to y=0.08 with x kept at ±0.06, because iteration 0's 5 cm look-ahead gave too little warning and this is the longest look-ahead the contract allows.

If steering_oscillation is high while max_error stays below 0.06 m, reduce the outer weights to ±0.75 (inner ±0.375), because iteration 0's outer weights of ±2 caused the overshoot and the Integrator's kp of 4.0 has been set to compensate for the lower weights.

Keep the body_width at 0.12 or wider, because the off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4), which stays at the 0.06 m floor for every allowed body width, so body changes cannot widen the margin in iteration 0's evidence.
